# Svc::Ccsds::TmFramer

<trecho source_id="src-cf097721f7a993df" chunk_id="chk-7923b727098a3ff8">
The `Svc::Ccsds::TmFramer` is an implementation of the [FramerInterface](../../../Interfaces/docs/sdd.md) for the CCSDS [TM Space Data Link Protocol](https://ccsds.org/Pubs/132x0b3.pdf). 
</trecho>

<trecho source_id="src-cf097721f7a993df" chunk_id="chk-ea35d9bc03f00ec9">
It receives a complete TM Transfer Frame Data Field (`Svc.Ccsds.TmDataFieldSize` bytes, produced by an upstream [`Svc::ComAggregator`](../../../ComAggregator/docs/sdd.md)) on input and produces a TM frame on its output port as a result. Please refer to the CCSDS [TM specification (CCSDS 132.0-B-3)](https://ccsds.org/Pubs/132x0b3.pdf) for details on the frame format and protocol.
</trecho>

<trecho source_id="src-cf097721f7a993df" chunk_id="chk-7153d66529edecb8">
The `Svc::Ccsds::TmFramer` is designed to work in the common F Prime telemetry stack, receiving complete, idle-filled data fields from an upstream [`Svc::ComAggregator`](../../../ComAggregator/docs/sdd.md) and passing frames to a [Communications Adapter](../../../Interfaces/docs/sdd.md), such as a Radio manager component or [`Svc::ComStub`](../../../ComStub/docs/sdd.md), for transmission on the wire. It is commonly coupled with the [`Svc::Ccsds::SpacePacketFramer`](../../SpacePacketFramer/docs/sdd.md) to wrap CCSDS Space Packets into TM frames.
</trecho>

<trecho source_id="src-cf097721f7a993df" chunk_id="chk-e099fe3f2f6fd619">
## Internals
</trecho>

<trecho source_id="src-cf097721f7a993df" chunk_id="chk-9b2a69020772515a">
The TM protocol specifies a fixed frame size. This can be configured in the `config/ComCfg.fpp` file.
</trecho>

Extraia requisitos, atores, componentes, entidades e relações dos trechos abaixo. Responda só com o objeto JSON.

<trecho source_id="src-cf097721f7a993df" chunk_id="chk-31173deed4796727">
The `Svc::Ccsds::TmFramer` uses an internal (member) buffer to hold the fixed size frame. The buffer **must** be returned to the TmFramer via the `dataReturnIn` port once it has been used or consumed. When the buffer returns to the TmFramer it will reuse the buffer for the next frame. Should a component want to use the frame data past the time it is returned to the TmFramer, data should be copied before the original buffer is returned to the TmFramer via the `dataReturnIn` port. 
</trecho>

<trecho source_id="src-cf097721f7a993df" chunk_id="chk-3876dd3a43021076">
The `Svc::Ccsds::TmFramer` is a pure frame layer: the data received on `dataIn` must fill the frame data field exactly (`Svc.Ccsds.TmDataFieldSize`, i.e. `ComCfg.TmFrameFixedSize` minus the 6-byte primary header and 2-byte trailer) and is copied into the frame unchanged. Any other size is rejected by assertion, deterministically on the first frame when the upstream stack is misconfigured. Idle filling of the data field (protocol 4.2.2.5) is the responsibility of the upstream [`Svc::ComAggregator`](../../../ComAggregator/docs/sdd.md), which emits aggregates of exactly its configured size; this keeps idle data upstream of any layer inserted between the aggregator and the framer, such as `Svc::Ccsds::CcsdsSdlsFramer`, whose added bytes (`Svc.Ccsds.SdlsSaIndexSize`) the project subtracts from the aggregation size.
</trecho>

The `Svc::Ccsds::AesGcmDecryptor` component decrypts and authenticates uplink data under AES-256-GCM, per CCSDS. It implements `Svc.Ccsds.CcsdsSdlsDecrypt` toward a decryption client (typically [`Svc::Ccsds::CcsdsSdlsDeframer`](../../CcsdsSdlsDeframer/docs/sdd.md) via [`Svc::Ccsds::SdlsSaRouter`](../../SdlsSaRouter/docs/sdd.md)) and `Svc.Ccsds.SdlsKeyInterfaceClient` toward a key supplier such as [`Svc::Ccsds::SdlsFileKeyManager`](../../SdlsFileKeyManager/docs/sdd.md). It is the security-providing alternative to [`Svc::Ccsds::ClearTextDecryptor`](../../ClearTextDecryptor/docs/sdd.md), and the uplink mirror of [`Svc::Ccsds::AesGcmEncryptor`](../../AesGcmEncryptor/docs/sdd.md).
</trecho>

<trecho source_id="src-e8a2e7c2f903f103" chunk_id="chk-382c724b03fdb281">
## Introduction
</trecho>

<trecho source_id="src-e8a2e7c2f903f103" chunk_id="chk-d12eaac6d5491aa4">
Decrypting a frame proceeds as follows:
</trecho>

<trecho source_id="src-e8a2e7c2f903f103" chunk_id="chk-264581ed660a571f">
1. Receive an SA index, ciphertext buffer (`IV (12) | ciphertext | MAC (16)`), and frame context on `decryptIn`.
2. Reject a buffer too short to hold an IV and a MAC with `DECRYPTION_FAILURE` — before requesting a key, since the uplink is attacker-influenced.
3. Request the AES-256 key for the frame's security association via `keyGet`; on failure or a wrong-sized key, report `KEY_ERROR`.
4. Decrypt in place, authenticating the SA index and virtual channel as AES-GCM additional authenticated data (AAD).
5. On a failed MAC check, report `MAC_VERIFICATION_FAILURE`, distinct from `DECRYPTION_FAILURE`; the component remains able to decrypt subsequent frames.
6. On success, narrow the buffer to the plaintext and emit it on `decryptOut` with status `SUCCESS`.
</trecho>

<trecho source_id="src-e8a2e7c2f903f103" chunk_id="chk-c4d16259adba9cea">
Decryption is in place, so the emitted buffer is the one received, advanced past the IV and narrowed to the plaintext length; `Fw::Buffer` keeps its allocation context independently of the data pointer, so it remains deallocatable by the issuing `Svc.BufferManager`. Buffers returned on `decryptReturnIn` are passed upstream via `bufferReturnOut` unconditionally, since every buffer emitted is the one that arrived.
</trecho>

## Security Considerations
</trecho>

<trecho source_id="src-e8a2e7c2f903f103" chunk_id="chk-b5ea28e4f0f7d55a">
What this component provides: confidentiality, integrity, and authentication of the frame body, bound to the SA index and the virtual channel. A frame modified in flight, built under a different key, or presented on a different virtual channel or SA fails the MAC check.
</trecho>

<trecho source_id="src-e8a2e7c2f903f103" chunk_id="chk-4deaadb2a13d70a1">
What it does not provide, and which an operator must plan for:
</trecho>

<trecho source_id="src-e8a2e7c2f903f103" chunk_id="chk-dde5709a4c20207d">
- **No anti-replay.** The IV is chosen by the sender and is not checked against anything, and no sequence number is tracked per SA. A previously valid TC frame captured off the link and re-injected later passes the MAC check and reaches the command path unchanged. SDLS anti-replay (CCSDS 355.0-B-2 §4.1.3) relies on an Anti-Replay Sequence Number in the security header, which this implementation does not carry. Missions exposed to a recording adversary need replay protection above this layer — a command counter, a time-bounded authorization window, or an idempotent command set.
- **No key rotation.** The key is fetched per frame from the connected key source, so rotation is that component's responsibility. The in-tree `Svc.Ccsds.SdlsFileKeyManager` serves one static key for the life of the process.
</trecho>

</item>

<item item_id="chk-cde31dc7861213ef" kind="source_chunk" source_id="src-e4ac13f99401393a" chunk_id="chk-cde31dc7861213ef">
For the APID usage of Packet IDs, I just want to call out a few things:
- 11 bit APID means there are only ~2048 to choose from (minus IDLE and other framework-utilized APIDs). And the APID domain is at the mission level. If we start thinking of multiple F´ deployments on a single bus, or even just F´ deployed as part of a broader spacecraft where the F´ deployment would be limited in terms of how many APIDs it's allocated... one could easily run out of APIDs. 
- I wouldn't say Packet ID is redundant with APID. TlmPacketizer currently utilizes a single APID, and can emit many different types of data within that APID. We're essentially multiplexing lots of data in a single APID by stamping out the Packet ID in the data. There's a bit of overhead to that yes, but it also has many benefits. Maybe the question we need to ask is what are we trying to optimize for?
- In a similar line of thought, one Packet ID == APID means a single space packet could only ever transmit a single Tlm Packet per Space Packet. No theoretical possibility of stuffing multiple Telemetry packets into a single Space Packet anymore. Is this desirable?
- Whatever direction we end up going, we will want to have a rationale for whether the downlinking of Events should have a format consistent with that of TlmPackets or not.
</item>
